en: And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Furat, who said: I heard Abu at-Tufayl narrating from Abu Sarihah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was in an upper room and we were beneath it talking... and he conveyed the hadith like it. Shu'bah said: And I think he said: 'It alights with them whenever they alight, and takes a midday rest with them wherever they take a midday rest.' Shu'bah said: And a man narrated this hadith to me from Abu at-Tufayl, from Abu Sarihah, and did not raise it to the Prophet; one of these two men said: 'the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam,' while the other said: 'a wind that casts them into the sea.'

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Furat al-Qazzaz, from Abu at-Tufayl, from Abu Sarihah, Hudhayfah ibn Asid, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was in an upper room while we were below him. He looked down upon us and said: 'What are you discussing?' We said: 'The Hour.' He said: 'Indeed, the Hour will not come until ten signs appear: a landslide in the east, a landslide in the west, and a landslide in the Arabian Peninsula; the smoke, the Dajjal, the beast of the earth, Gog and Magog, the rising of the sun from its place of setting, and a fire that emerges from the depths of Aden driving the people.' Shu'bah said: And 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay' narrated to me from Abu at-Tufayl, from Abu Sarihah, the like of that, not mentioning the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); and one of the two said regarding the tenth: 'the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him),' while the other said: 'and a wind that casts the people into the sea.'

Abu Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar al-Makki narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's; Ishaq said: 'informed us', and the other two said: 'narrated to us'—Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Furat al-Qazzaz, from Abu at-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) looked out upon us while we were discussing, and said: 'What are you discussing?' They said: 'We are discussing the Hour.' He said: 'It will never be established until you see ten signs before it.' And he mentioned the smoke, the Dajjal, the beast, the rising of the sun from its place of setting, the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), Gog and Magog, and three landslides: a landslide in the east, a landslide in the west, and a landslide in the Arabian Peninsula; and the last of that is a fire that emerges from Yemen, driving the people to their place of gathering.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, from Nafi' ibn 'Utbah, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on an expedition. He said: A people from the direction of the west, wearing woollen garments, came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and met him near a hillock. They were standing while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was seated. He said: My soul said to me: 'Go to them and stand between them and him lest they assassinate him!' He said: Then I said: 'Perhaps he is conferring privately with them.' So I went to them and stood between them and him. He said: And I memorized four statements from him which I count on my fingers. He said: 'You will invade the Arabian Peninsula and Allah will open it; then Persia and Allah will open it; then you will invade Rome and Allah will open it; then you will invade the Dajjal and Allah will conquer him.' He said: Nafi' said: 'O Jabir, we do not think the Dajjal will emerge until Rome has been conquered.'

And Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Sulayman—meaning Ibn al-Mughirah—narrated to us: Humayd—meaning Ibn Hilal—narrated to us, from Abu Qatadah, from Usayr ibn Jabir, who said: I was in the house of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and the house was full. He said: Then a red wind blew in Kufa... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Ibn 'Ulayyah.

Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated to me: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Qatadah, from Yusayr ibn Jabir, who said: I was with Ibn Mas'ud when a red wind blew... and he conveyed the hadith in a similar manner. And the hadith of Ibn 'Ulayyah is more complete and fuller.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us, both from Ibn 'Ulayyah—and the wording is Ibn Hujr's: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Qatadah al-'Adawi, from Yusayr ibn Jabir, who said: A red wind blew violently in Kufa, and a man came having no other cry except: 'O 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, the Hour has come!' He said: So he sat up, having been reclining, and said: 'Indeed, the Hour will not be established until no inheritance is divided and no spoil brings joy.' Then he gestured with his hand like this—pointing it toward ash-Sham—and said: 'An enemy will gather against the people of Islam, and the people of Islam will gather against them.' I said: 'Do you mean the Byzantines?' He said: 'Yes, and during that battle there will be fierce retreating and advancing. The Muslims will send forth a vanguard pledged to death, not to return unless victorious. They will fight until the night intervenes between them, so both sides will return, neither being victorious, and the vanguard will have perished. Then the Muslims will send forth a vanguard pledged to death, not to return unless victorious. They will fight until the night intervenes between them, so both sides will return, neither being victorious, and the vanguard will have perished. Then the Muslims will send forth a vanguard pledged to death, not to return unless victorious. They will fight until evening comes, so both sides will return, neither being victorious, and the vanguard will have perished. When the fourth day arrives, the remainder of the people of Islam will advance against them, and Allah will make defeat fall upon the enemy, so they will slaughter them with a slaughter—either he said: the like of which has never been seen, or: the like of which was never seen—such that a bird passing by their flanks will not clear them before it drops dead. The sons of one father, who were 100, will count their numbers and find that none of them remains except 1 man. So with what spoils could anyone rejoice, or what inheritance could be divided? While they are in that state, they will hear of a calamity greater than that: a crier will come shouting that the Dajjal has taken their place among their offspring. So they will cast aside what is in their hands and advance, sending forth 10 horsemen as an advance guard.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, I know their names, the names of their fathers, and the colors of their horses; they will be the best horsemen on the face of the earth on that day—or among the best horsemen on the face of the earth on that day.' Ibn Abi Shaybah said in his narration: from Usayr ibn Jabir.

Harmalah ibn Yahya at-Tujibi narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Abu Shurayh narrated to me that 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith narrated to him that al-Mustawrid al-Qurashi said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'The Hour will be established while the Byzantines are the most numerous of people.' He said: That reached 'Amr ibn al-'As, so he said: 'What are these hadiths mentioned about you that you say them from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?' Al-Mustawrid said to him: 'I only said what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' 'Amr said: 'If you say that, indeed they are the most clement of people during turmoil, the quickest to recover from a calamity, and the best of people to their poor and their weak.'

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to me: al-Layth ibn Sa'd informed me: Musa ibn 'Ulayy narrated to me, from his father, who said: Al-Mustawrid al-Qurashi said in the presence of 'Amr ibn al-'As: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: 'The Hour will be established while the Byzantines are the most numerous of people.' 'Amr said to him: 'Look to what you are saying!' He said: 'I am saying what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' He said: 'If you say that, indeed they possess four characteristics: they are the most clement of people during turmoil, the quickest to recover after a calamity, the swiftest to rally after retreating in battle, and the best of them to the poor, orphan, and weak; and a fifth characteristic that is fine and beautiful: they are the most resistant to the oppression of kings.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Mu'alla ibn Mansur narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us: Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until the Byzantines alight at al-A'maq or Dabiq. Then an army from Medina, consisting of the best people of the earth on that day, will go out to meet them. When they form their ranks, the Byzantines will say: "Leave us and those who took captives from us so that we may fight them!" But the Muslims will say: "No, by Allah, we will never leave you and our brothers!" So they will fight them: one third will flee, whom Allah will never forgive; one third will be killed, who are the best martyrs in the sight of Allah; and one third will conquer, never to be afflicted by trials, and they will conquer Constantinople. While they are dividing the spoils, having hung their swords on olive trees, Satan will cry out among them: "The False Messiah has taken your place among your families!" So they will go out, but that will be false. When they reach ash-Sham, he will emerge. While they are preparing for battle, straightening their ranks, the prayer will be called, and 'Isa ibn Maryam will descend and lead them. When the enemy of Allah sees him, he will dissolve just as salt dissolves in water. If he were to leave him, he would dissolve until he perished, but Allah will kill him with his hand, showing them his blood upon his spear.'

'Ubayd ibn Ya'ish and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is 'Ubayd's—both saying: Yahya ibn Adam ibn Sulayman, freed slave of Khalid ibn Khalid, narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Iraq withheld its dirham and its qafiz, ash-Sham withheld its mudy and its dinar, Egypt withheld its irdabb and its dinar, and you reverted to where you began, you reverted to where you began, you reverted to where you began!' The flesh and blood of Abu Hurayrah testified to that.

Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn and Abu Ma'n ar-Raqashi narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Ma'n's—both saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us: my father informed me, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, who said: I was standing with Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and he said: 'People will not cease stretching their necks in pursuit of the world.' I said: 'Yes indeed.' He said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "The Euphrates will soon uncover a mountain of gold. When the people hear of it, they will head towards it, and those by it will say: 'If we leave people to take from it, all of it will certainly be taken away.' He said: So they will fight over it, and out of every 100, 99 will be killed."' Abu Kamil said in his hadith: He said: 'I and Ubayy ibn Ka'b stood in the shade of Hassan's fortress.'

Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us: 'Uqbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah, from Abu az-Zinad, from 'Abd ar-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Euphrates will soon uncover a mountain of gold, so whoever is present at it should not take anything from it.'

Abu Mas'ud, Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us: 'Uqbah ibn Khalid as-Sakuni narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah, from Khubayb ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Euphrates will soon uncover a treasure of gold, so whoever is present at it should not take anything from it.'

And Umayyah ibn Bistam narrated to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Rawh narrated to us, from Suhayl, with this chain of narration, the like of it, and he added: 'So my father said: "If you see it, do not approach it!"'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The Hour will not be established until the Euphrates uncovers a mountain of gold over which the people will fight, so that out of every 100, 99 will be killed, and each man among them will say: "Perhaps I will be the one who survives!"'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us, both saying: Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: Jundab said: I arrived on the day of al-Jara'ah, and behold, there was a man sitting, so I said: 'Blood will surely be spilled here today!' That man said: 'By no means, by Allah!' I said: 'Yes indeed, by Allah!' He said: 'By no means, by Allah!' I said: 'Yes indeed, by Allah!' He said: 'By no means, by Allah! Indeed, it is a hadith of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) which he narrated to me.' I said: 'What a wretched companion you have been to me all day, hearing me contradict you while you heard it from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), yet you did not restrain me!' Then I said: 'What is this anger?' So I turned to him to question him, and behold, the man was Hudhayfah.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ad-Dawraqi and Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to me, both from Abu 'Asim—Hajjaj said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us: 'Azrah ibn Thabit informed us: 'Ilba' ibn Ahmar informed us: Abu Zayd—meaning 'Amr ibn Akhtab—narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) led us in the Fajr prayer, then climbed the pulpit and addressed us until the time for Dhuhr arrived. Then he descended and prayed. Then he climbed the pulpit and addressed us until the time for 'Asr arrived. Then he descended and prayed. Then he climbed the pulpit and addressed us until the sun set. Thus he informed us of what had been and what was to be; so the most knowledgeable among us is the one with the best memory.
Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me: Shu'bah informed us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us [H]; and Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated to me: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn Yazid, from Hudhayfah, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) informed me of what will happen until the Hour is established, so there was nothing of it except that I asked him about it, except that I did not ask him what will drive the people of Medina out of Medina.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration, up to his words: 'and forgotten by whoever forgot it,' and he did not mention what came after it.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—'Uthman said: 'narrated to us', and Ishaq said: 'informed us'—Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood before us in an address and did not leave out anything that would happen from that position of his until the establishment of the Hour except that he narrated it: memorized by whoever memorized it and forgotten by whoever forgot it. These companions of mine certainly know it; and indeed something of it might occur that I had forgotten, but when I see it, I remember it just as a man remembers the face of a man who had been absent from him, then when he sees him, he recognizes him.

Harmalah ibn Yahya at-Tujibi narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Abu Idris al-Khawlani used to say: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: 'By Allah, I am indeed the most knowledgeable of people concerning every tribulation that will occur between me and the Hour. It is not because the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) confided to me something secret concerning that which he did not narrate to anyone else; but rather, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) spoke while narrating about tribulations to a gathering in which I was present. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said while enumerating the tribulations: "Among them are three that will hardly leave anything behind, and among them are tribulations like the winds of summer, some small and some great."' Hudhayfah said: 'All of that group have departed except me.'

And Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated it to us: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn Hakim al-Ansari narrated to us: 'Amir ibn Sa'd informed me, from his father, that he approached with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) among a group of his companions, and passed by the mosque of Banu Mu'awiyah... the like of the hadith of Ibn Numayr.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us [H]; and Ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is his: my father narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us: 'Amir ibn Sa'd informed me, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came one day from the high ground of Medina. When he passed by the mosque of Banu Mu'awiyah, he entered and prayed two rak'ahs in it, and we prayed with him. He supplicated his Lord for a long time, then turned to us and said (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): 'I asked my Lord for three things, and He granted me two and withheld one from me: I asked my Lord not to destroy my Ummah with widespread famine, and He granted it to me; and I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted it to me; and I asked Him not to make their strife among themselves, but He withheld it from me.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to me—Ishaq said: 'informed us', and the others said: 'narrated to us'—Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma' ar-Rahabi, from Thawban, that the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, folded up the earth for me until I saw its eastern and western extremities, and He gave me the two treasures: the red and the white...' then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Ayyub from Abu Qilabah.

Abu ar-Rabi' al-'Ataki and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both from Hammad ibn Zayd—and the wording is Qutaybah's: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, Allah folded up the earth for me, so I saw its eastern and western extremities; and indeed the dominion of my Ummah will reach whatever was folded up for me of it. And I was given the two treasures: the red and the white. And indeed I asked my Lord for my Ummah that He not destroy them by widespread famine, and that He not give power over them to an enemy from other than their own selves who would eradicate their main body. And indeed my Lord said: "O Muhammad, when I decree a matter, it is never turned back; and I have granted you for your Ummah that I will not destroy them with widespread famine, and that I will not give power over them to an enemy from other than their own selves who would eradicate their main body, even if those from all regions of the earth—or He said: from between its regions—were to gather against them, until some of them destroy one another and take one another captive."'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah [H]; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: 'When two Muslims, one of them bears arms against his brother, they are both on the brink of Hellfire; and if one of them kills his companion, they will both enter it.'

Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us from his book: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, with this chain of narration, the like of the hadith of Abu Kamil from Hammad, to its end.

And Ahmad ibn 'Abdah ad-Dabbi narrated it to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, Yunus, and al-Mu'alla ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from Abu Bakrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, both the killer and the killed are in the Fire.'
